title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
description:
You are given an array of strings `tokens` that represents an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation (postfix notation).

Evaluate the expression and return an integer representing its value.

Note that:
- The valid operators are `'+'`, `'-'`, `'*'`, and `'/'`.
- Each operand may be an integer or another expression.
- Division between two integers always truncates toward zero (for example, `7 / -2 = -3` and `-7 / 2 = -3`).
- There will not be any division by zero.
- The input represents a valid arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation.
- The answer and all intermediate calculations can be represented in a 32-bit signed integer.
constraints: tokens[i] is either an operator ("+", "-", "*", or "/") or an integer in the range [-200, 200].
The input represents a valid arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation.
Division by zero never occurs, and all intermediate and final results fit in a 32-bit signed integer.
hints: In Reverse Polish Notation, every operator applies to the two most recent operands.
Maintain a stack of integer values: push numbers onto the stack, and on an operator pop the right operand first, then the left operand, apply the operator, and push the result back.
Be careful with subtraction and division operand order (left op right) and ensure division truncates toward zero rather than flooring toward negative infinity.
